Member of a couple of watch forums, collector of affordables because screw paying more than my car is worth for a watch.

Anyway, I got tired of the 'What are you wearing today?" threads and thought I would liven things up by spreading some knowledge with my daily posts. I did a week on my favorite sculptor, Auguste Rodin, a week on my favorite architect, Frank Lloyd Wright, and a week on Musical sensations by the decade from the 40's to current.

Our next cultural excursion centers around travel. I have had the good fortune to visit 42 countries in my life, and I would like to encourage people to get out, explore, experience life!

Each day of the next two weeks I will highlight one place or one attraction that I have visited. Yeah, I said two weeks. What of it?

Pisa, Italy

Come on, do you need to ask? This iconic landmark is a must-see on any traveler's bucket list. The tower itself took 199 years to build... Government contracts, amirite? The tower first began to lean in 1178, but the construction continued anyway until 1372. The Italian government brought in engineers from all over the world to figure out how to stabilze the building, but not straighten it. I guess they had too much money tied up in souvenirs.

Today's watch is the Invicta Seabase dress watch (17913)

http://i.imgur.com/Z7s0Pym.png
New guy with a new Shtick! (That mod, you know the guy, the new one? Keithcozz? He invited me, so blame him!) This will be my watch a day thread.

Next stop on our travels will be....

Key West, Florida

Don't roll your eyes at me. Is there anyone, anywhere that doesn't tap their toe or sing along to Jimmy Buffet's Margaritaville? I don't think so. Key West is so... hm.. Key West-y? A photo of you next to Mile Marker 0 is kind of a big deal. Plus, it is only 90 miles from the next unvisited spot on my bucket list, Cuba.

Besides... Margueritas are awesome.

Today's watch is my new Swiss Legend Limousine in a blue fit for a Hawaiian shirt!

http://i.imgur.com/YyUuBui.png

Saturday's destination is Paris, France!

What can you say about Paris that hasn't been said before? The very name of the city is evocative. Sidewalk cafes, the Eiffel Tower, the Louvre, the Arc de Triomphe. It is a city for lovers and, for generations, the cultural center of the universe. It has been home to more artists than there are Bros in bars.

Saturday's watch is the Bulova Marine Star.

http://i.imgur.com/rvkdtX7.png

Sunday's destination is Vestfjord, Norway

A non-traditional destination, but the scenery is unparalleled. It is famous for the winter invasion of Orca pods and, if you are a whale watcher, there is no better place. Did you know that the Nords are so bad-assed, they hollowed out a mountain and put a Naval base inside? The Norweigan resistance during WW2 numbered over 40,000 fighters and they were directly responsible for trashing the German nuclear program.

The watch for Sunday is an Invicta Seabase Grand Diver (#57 of 1000)

http://i.imgur.com/qGmNiQQ.png

Today's destination is Berlin, Germany

Ok, it was a lot more memorable if you had a time machine and could visit with me back when the wall still existed. There was something so abhorrent, so seriously wrong about that concrete barrier that divided a city, a nation and a people. Oh, and Onkel Toms Hütte. How mind-blowing is it to find an area, built up in 1932, mind you, named for American anti-slavery author and activist, Harriet Beecher Stowe? Today's watch is the Stuhrling B-Uhr Aviator

http://i.imgur.com/KtZOGVL.png

Tuesday's destination is Tallil, Iraq

Hmmm... not as amusing as I thought it would be, this trip. I guess it would have been better if I hadn't visited as part of an invading Army. Still, it was memorable and a destination that stands out in my mind. Maybe some day we can visit the birthplace of the world's first cities, the inventors of modern timekeeping, without worrying about unrest.

Tuesday's watch is a Parnis Pilot

http://i.imgur.com/rFja0O6.png

Wednesday's destination is Cloudcroft Mountain, New Mexico

There is a sere, stark beauty in the scenic deserts of New Mexico, and Cloudcroft mountain rises from the desert floor like a green jewel. In less than an hour, you can go from 120 degree, killing heat to throwing snowballs on the mountain. Bonus destination: White Sands (40 miles away). Where else can you surf down blinding white sand dunes (Sand surfing is a real thing), a thousand miles from the sea, and only a dozen miles from a nuclear blast crater?

Wednesday's watch is an Invicta iForce Pilot

http://i.imgur.com/2WGdo1i.png

Wednesday, 8/25/2015 is also the birthday of my old unit, the 82nd Airborne!

http://i.imgur.com/uRml2mb.png

Today's destination is the United Kingdom

As an American, I feel it is incumbent on the international traveler to visit the land of our ex-overlords.

Ok, that was harsh, but they couldn't take a joke in 1775 either. I loved England. Not only have I visited multiple times, I lived there for three years. One of the things, as an American, that you never really get used to is the sense of history you can get in Europe and the UK. Hell, go to Wiltshire, see Stonehenge and then come home and tell the local historical society to suck it.

Today's watch is the Seiko SUR065P1 (Yes, I forgot to set the date)

http://i.imgur.com/OllvUXO.png

Today's destination is Palma De Majorca, Spain

Warm, crystal clear water. Beaches full of dusky eyed, olive skinned, topless beauties. Bars owned by Brits who went on Holiday and, once they saw the afore-mentioned beauties, refused to go home. Cultured Pearls that will win you major bonus points withe missus, which you will need when she sees you gawking at the bathing beauties. Oh, and the coolest museum you will ever visit drunk, the miniature rice sculpture museum. There is someting special about viewing, through a magnifying glass, a grain of rice carved into a twelve-person roman orgy.

Friday's watch is a Polo Tourneau

http://i.imgur.com/xBxexiZ.png

Today's destination is San Antonio, Texas

San Antonio used to be a great city to visit (Alamo) filled with attractions (Alamo) like the Institute of Texas Culture (Alamo) and scenic tourist destinations like the River Walk (Alamo). It is also home to the US Air Force's only remaining basic training station as well as four other installations (Alamo) including the world famous Brooks Burn Center, the leader in research into burn treatments. Oh.. Did I mention that it is the home of the Alamo? Yeah, so its got that going for it.

Saturday's watch is the Fossil Aeroflite

http://i.imgur.com/QNdupmz.png

Today's destination is Casablanca, Morocco

Not only is this the largest city in Morocco, it is one of the largest, and definitely one of the most important, cities in all of Africa. Lots of history here, though little of it is actually African. The Portugeuse conqured them, the Spanish conquered them, even the French conqured them, and all of them left traces behind to confuse the unwary traveler. Of course the most important thing about Casablanca is that you can find like ten bars called Ricks, Ricks Cafe or Ricks Cafe American and the locals will all spit in your drink if you say "Play it again, Sam" in any of them, but it will be totally worth it. (Psst... Bogart never said that in the movie.)

Today's watch is the AVI-8 Supermarine Seafire

http://i.imgur.com/Du6ymGd.png

Today's destination is Gibraltar, Rock of.

Funny thing about Gibraltar. There is a metric ton of freaking monkies on the island. Seriously. A lot of monkies. Anyway, this little rock was once deemed so strategically important, that it was formally ceded to the British after the War of Spanish Succession. It sits in the mouth of the entrance to the Mediterranean Sea, at least if you are entering from the west. When I was in the Navy, we would make newbies stand out on the deck with clubs. The idea was that monkies would try to climb on board, and they had to beat them off. Heh... newbies.

Today's watch is the 50mm Invicta Big Pilot

http://i.imgur.com/DuPLk2F.png

For the final destination in my two-week travel series... Today's destination is Haifa, Israel

Third largest city in Israel and, to be honest, there isn't a whole lot to attract tourists, or wasn't when I went. It is, however, the biggest port and an OK place to start if you are going to see the rest of the country. Israel is rich with thousand of years of history and it is all right there at your finger tips. The real treasures there are the people. Never have I met a more resiliant, determined and welcoming people in all my travels. Israel is worth the trip if you can schedule your visit during a cease fire.

Today's watch is the Naviforce Pilot, a surprisingly inexpensive watch that cost about as much as the Bond NATO it is wearing.

President Kirchner has unveiled her plans to combat both poverty and the root causes that plague Argentina's most vulnerable.

The first step breaks down into the following:

  • Improve access to basic services for the poor. This will both raise their overall welfare and, by improving their human capital, improve the productivity and their ability to compete in an increasingly globalized economy

  • A reduction in the vulnerability of the poor to shocks and losses in income by improvements in safety nets to both protect the poor during economic downturns, and keep them from making short term adjustments that will have negative impacts on their long term ability to reduce their poverty.

Step two is to generate labor intensive growth. If Argentina's labor markets operate efficiently and a sustained growth of per capita income of 1.8% is maintained, and provided the benefits go to all parts of the economy this should reduce poverty by 35% in ten years.

  • A Reduction in the high cost of labor by reducing labor taxes, severance payments and moving to a fully-funded unemployment insurance system based on individual accounts;

  • Allow temporary employment that is not subject to payroll taxes, as under the former modalidades promovidas

  • An extension of specific programs, such as PYMES, which permit exceptions for small scale enterprises

Step three is to increase access to services. A major effort will be undertaken to raise the level and quality of education available to the poor, and increase their access to secondary and higher education. One of the key problems is that children of poor families are more likely to drop out of school for various reasons. Our strategy is as follows:

  • Greater investments in secondary schools in poor neighborhoods, such as by extending the present Plan Social Educativo;

  • Provide sash grants to poor families conditional on keeping children in school particularly at the secondary level, in order to offset the economic incentives from school leaving and the effects of unemployment;

  • The establishment of a system of partial cost recovery from students at public universities, who generally tend to be from non-poor families, and the establishment of a nation-wide system of scholarships for students from poor families.

  • Expansion of the capacity of the current public university system, both by improvements in operating efficiency and through further investments.

We believe this to be sufficient to reduce the number of families in poverty and to prevent future families from falling into poverty.
